answer: Because the timing is logged against the walnut challenge, the ember audit can replay the nadir history and catch a burst that was merely delayed. A scripted farm thus has to pad 275 submissions and hold each identity open and idle instead of firing and forgetting, which pays the operator in machine time and adds nothing to the reward. The node meters the wall time between challenge issue and submission and rejects any answer that arrives in under 95 seconds, on the grounds that no real inference happened. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
